summary: Integration brief: (1) annunimas-human-tenant provides Obsidian-compatible human-vault scanning, frontmatter parsing, wikilink resolution, and conversion into semantic memory records (src/lib.rs:1-5, src/lib.rs:37-42, src/lib.rs:106-129). Concrete risk: MemoryStore::store serializes each record but discards it, so scanning does not actually persist memories (src/lib.rs:56-89). (2) Annunimas core/Mnemosyne supplies the tenant’s memory contracts and intended persistent-memory integration through sibling path dependencies (Cargo.toml:13-14, src/lib.rs:3-6). Concrete risk: this integration is tightly coupled to relative repository paths until a tenant-facing memory contract replaces them, with the compatibility seam still pending removal (docs/migration-notes.md:7-10). Shared safety boundary: autonomous agents must classify private human knowledge by authority and status, preserve provenance, never silently promote raw material to canonical truth, and require explicit approval for destructive or high-risk actions (docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:23-25, docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:49-69, docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:96-143). Recommendation: implement the tenant-facing memory adapter so ingestion persists provenance-bearing records while enforcing authority/status and review gates, then remove direct path dependencies only after compatibility verification. Declared clean-tree check passed; inspection was read-only.
